content: 1. Spray solutions should be prepared only in quantities that are immediately required to avoid wastage and potential environmental contamination. 2. Pesticide containers must be triple-rinsed and crushed prior to disposal, with the rinsate being incorporated into the spray solution to minimize waste. 3. Proper disposal of pesticide containers and unused pesticides must strictly adhere to the instructions provided on the pesticide labels. 4. Licensed Pest Control Operators (PCOs) are legally obligated to follow national regulations when disposing of unwanted pesticides and containers, ensuring that human and animal safety is not compromised and that the environment, including waterways and water supplies, is not contaminated. 5. For detailed guidance on managing pesticide waste and empty containers, reference materials published by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Health Organization (WHO) are recommended. 6. In the event of pesticide leaks or spills, licensed PCOs must take immediate and appropriate action to contain the spillage or leakage, following national guidelines. The spilled material must be disposed of properly, and the incident should be reported to the relevant Pest Control Licensing Department (PCOLD). 7. PCO license renewals should be applied for a specified number of months (e.g., two months) before the license expires. 8. Attendance at refresher courses may be a prerequisite for license renewal, and in some countries, passing an examination for recertification is also required. 9. The PCOLD must ensure timely renewal of licenses to prevent disruption in the work of PCOs. 10. Individuals who are not fully qualified to operate as PCOs may be employed as Assistant Pest Control Operators (APCOs) to assist with less technical tasks. 11. A separate APCO license should be created to meet this demand, and licensed APCOs must work under the supervision of a licensed PCO. 12. Applicants for an APCO license must meet basic requirements, including being at least 18 years old, possessing the minimum educational qualifications as determined by the licensing authority, completing the prescribed training course, passing the mandatory examination, and undergoing a pre-placement medical examination. 13. APCO licenses are issued for a specified period (e.g., x years) and must include a badge license and a written section detailing the conditions of the license. 14. APCO license holders must wear their licenses during pest control operations. 15. APCO license renewals require submission of applications a specified number of months before expiry, and attendance at refresher courses may be mandated. 16. Provisions should be made for upgrading an APCO license to a PCO license, requiring active work as an APCO for a minimum number of years and successful completion of the prescribed PCO training and examination. 17. The PCOLD is responsible for ensuring that pest control activities are conducted properly and do not adversely affect public health, safety, or the environment. 18. The PCOLD must effectively implement and enforce PCO regulations, ensuring adequate planning, training, and certification before licensing regulations come into effect. 19. Enforcement of licensing regulations is critical to discourage violations that could harm public health or the environment. 20. Qualified inspectors with the authority to inspect premises, vehicles, records, and operations, as well as investigate complaints and impose penalties, should be appointed to serve the PCOLD. 21. Inspectors must prepare reports of their inspections and investigations for review and action by the PCOLD management. 22. The PCOLD should have the authority to suspend, cancel, or withdraw licenses for violations of regulations or licensing conditions, following a thorough review of inspection reports. 23. Provisions for appeals against suspension, cancellation, or non-issuance of licenses should be included in the regulations. 24. The PCOLD is responsible for conducting certification courses for PCOs and APCOs, potentially in collaboration with other organizations or academic institutions. 25. Training courses should emphasize practical aspects of pest management and be reviewed periodically to incorporate the latest developments and best practices. 26. PCOs handling fumigants must attend specialized courses and pass mandatory examinations before being authorized to perform fumigation work. 27. Certification examinations should be conducted at least annually, with details widely publicized at least six months in advance. 28. The PCOLD must ensure that licensed PCOs and APCOs undergo pre-placement and periodic medical examinations to safeguard their health and establish baseline physical condition records. 29. Medical surveillance reports conducted under occupational health and safety legislation should be accepted in the licensing process. 30. The PCOLD should maintain impartiality and transparency in its licensing decisions and actions, forming committees to evaluate and approve applications. 31. Inspectors should be periodically relocated to different areas of responsibility to ensure fair enforcement of regulations. 32. Training for PCOLD officers should include policies on conflict of interest and ethics to maintain integrity. 33. PCOs should form professional associations to promote professionalism and cooperation between the industry and regulators. 34. A code of ethics should be introduced, emphasizing safe and efficient pest control practices, environmental considerations, and the importance of Integrated Vector Management (IVM). 35. Licensees must be made aware of what constitutes an offense under the regulations to avoid violations. 36. Penalties for non-compliance should be clearly stipulated in the legislation and fairly enforced to encourage self-regulation within the industry. 37. Minor offenses may be addressed with verbal or written warnings, followed by fines, suspension, or license revocation for repeated or severe violations. 38. On-the-spot fines for minor offenses may be implemented in some countries to reduce court costs, but strict caution is required to prevent abuse of this process.
